events.continuity_hook: Carry the strongest outbound and return options into a hotel search once the venue is confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare practical round-trip itineraries and identify two candidates that satisfy the meeting schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus needs a round-trip flight from Chicago to Atlanta for a two-day regional leadership meeting in mid-April. He must arrive before a 2:00 p.m. opening session on Monday and can leave after 5:30 p.m. Tuesday; the meeting venue and exact return cutoff are still unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the selected flight candidates while narrowing lodging and checking whether Tuesday luggage storage will be needed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare a compact set of nearby hotels on total cost, transit effort, cancellation terms, and Tuesday luggage handling.
events.scenario_brief: The Atlanta meeting is now confirmed near the Georgia World Congress Center, and Marcus needs one hotel night within an easy walk or a short direct ride. His employer's nightly reimbursement cap is now known, but late checkout availability and the final meeting end time remain unclear.

events.continuity_hook: Record the confirmed itinerary so a later schedule issue can be handled without rebuilding the trip.
events.interaction_goal: Validate the door-to-door timing, confirm the chosen flight and hotel details, and complete the reservations.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus is ready to finalize the Atlanta trip after learning that Tuesday's meeting will end at 4:30 p.m. He has chosen a nearby hotel and needs the flight times checked against travel to and from the venue before both reservations are completed.

events.continuity_hook: Use the better date window as the basis for a deeper neighborhood and room comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two date windows at a high level and identify which offers the more workable combination of flight schedules, trip length, and lodging supply.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus and his husband are considering San Diego for their family's main coastal vacation in late July, traveling from Chicago with their 12-year-old son for seven or eight nights. School dates permit either of two adjacent departure weekends, and they want to understand how airfare and lodging availability differ before choosing exact dates; their trip budget has not yet been divided between flights and hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Carry two lodging finalists forward so flight selection can be evaluated alongside airport-to-hotel logistics and full trip cost.
events.interaction_goal: Build a detailed comparison of suitable rooms in both areas and narrow the choice to two properties with verified occupancy terms.
events.scenario_brief: The family has settled on a Saturday-to-Sunday eight-night window and is weighing Coronado against La Jolla. They need a room that clearly accommodates two adults and one child, and Marcus wants to compare beach access, parking costs, and travel time to planned visits at the zoo and Balboa Park; no property has been selected.

events.continuity_hook: Use the selected itinerary to choose between the two hotels and prepare the family trip for booking in a later session.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the viable flight options for all three travelers and determine whether the earlier arrival justifies its added total cost.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus has narrowed the stay to one Coronado property and one La Jolla property, both currently cancellable, and now needs round-trip flights for three travelers on the chosen dates. One outbound option arrives early enough to preserve most of Saturday but costs more, while a lower-cost itinerary arrives in the evening; ground travel from the airport and the effect on the first hotel night remain unresolved.
